correctness.rationale: The continuous-time reset generator gives the homogeneous recurrence off 0, with π_n=π_0. The two roots x<1<y have xy=p/q; the positive unnormalized profile x^j/(1−x^n)+y^j/(y^n−1) takes the same value at j=0 and n, satisfies the recurrence, and the last balance equation follows by conservation. Irreducibility makes this the unique stationary law. For the hopping-only current, dividing the negative root contribution by the positive one gives R_j=x^(n−2j−1)F_j with F_j=h^(j+1)(1−x)(1−x^n)/[(h−x)(h^n−x^n)], h=p/q. At fixed x, F_j(1,x)=1 and ∂_h log F_j<(j+1−n)/h−1/(h−x)<0. Thus nonnegative exponent implies a permanently positive current, including exponent zero. For negative exponent, log R_j is strictly decreasing in x with nonzero derivative: both rational factor derivatives after grouping are negative, as is the power term. Since x′(r)<0 and x goes from 1 to 0, R_j increases from zero to infinity with a simple unit crossing. R_(j+1)/R_j=h/x²>1 then gives strict reversed ordering of the rates, exactly floor(n/2) distinct crossings and the contiguous counterflow arc. For the small-bias expansion, analyticity follows by solving the normalized finite system near δ=r=0 after scaling rates by q. The r-derivative of the current at zero bias obeys a_j−a_(j−1)=−1/n and Σa_j=0, while J_j(δ,0)=δ/n. The implicit-function slope is therefore 2/(2j+1−n), positive on each reversing edge; the error is O(δ²/q) for fixed n,j,q, not uniform in n. Independently bisected actual stationary currents for the n=6 example by pivoted Gaussian elimination on the nonreset balance equations and normalization (r bracket [0,5]); edges 5,4,3 gave 0.226733124762156, 0.484739267504340, 3.435620322241912. These floating-point examples are ancillary. The submitted rational checker and verification notes were inspected without executing the uploaded code.

The Li–Sun publisher summary reports biased-network stationary distribution and first-passage formulas, but full text was not inspectable.

They do not in the inspected statements give a parameter-wise sign or simple-zero theorem for every individual hopping edge. Their specialization is not itself the crossing classification.

evidence: Stationary conservation by itself orders currents in space at a fixed r; spectral density expressions can produce their values. Neither conservation alone nor the inspected one-way, symmetric and membrane examples state rate-wise monotonic crossing of the hopping current ratio.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The key new inference concerns variation in r, not merely spatial decrease at each fixed r. The strictly signed grouped derivative on one half, the separate exclusion on the other half and the weak-bias limit are needed to turn the stationary law into the ordered all-edge classification. The inspected results do not mechanically give these conclusions.

evidence: Rose et al. use one-way hopping in their ring example; Riascos et al. use a symmetric ring. Tucci et al. show the reset path changes the total ring current without changing the stationary spatial law.
Resultary f8d346c6a6a6 studies membrane current on a biased Brownian ring with resetting supported in one semicircle.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The physical edge observable is pπ_j−qπ_(j+1), not a current conserved by counting a chosen reset path, nor global velocity or membrane flow. Rescaling by q or reversing the ring orientation leaves the problem equivalent but does not identify it with a one-way, symmetric, or continuum model.

evidence: 29407f68bac2 is the assigned record itself, not independent prior work. The distinct same-day f8d346c6a6a6 record gives one or no reversals of a Brownian membrane current; c2705ab73d30 concerns reversal of global velocity in a periodic Brownian ratchet.
The exact finite-ring example in Rose et al. has q=0 and hence positive hopping flow on all edges for finite r.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: For a continuously parameterized theorem the material exact match would be an all-rate analytic threshold classification, rather than a finite numerical table. These items do not give an exact threshold sequence for the frozen model; the similar same-day theorem was compared by observable and dynamics, not chronologically dismissed.

originality.rationale: The general reset stationary representation and ideas of current reversal are prior background. The distinct supported result is the global, all-size and all-edge record of simple hopping-only crossings with strict rate ordering and weak-bias thresholds. The closest discrete and continuum statements do not supply that classification. This is a bounded best-of-knowledge comparison, not a priority certificate.

value.rationale: The model is a canonical nonequilibrium ring with one reset destination. The result explains precisely how local physical hopping can flow against the global clockwise bias even though the total hopping current remains positive. It proves absence of hidden or repeated local crossings and gives a sharp spatial and rate sequence and its near-equilibrium scale, none of which follows from forward stationary probabilities or conservation alone. The observable remains tied to actual hopping transitions and does not depend on assigning paths to teleportation.
